# Shell

<!-- Generated by `prism docs` from `lib/std/Shell.pr`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Shell: a small vocabulary for script-shaped programs, over `Proc` and `Path`.

Nothing here is a second process model. A command is still a `Proc.Command`, adjusted with the modifiers below, and every run is still one `Proc` step: `run` checks the status and keeps what a script needs to report a failure, `run_text` and `run_lines` decode the output, and `pipe` runs a pipeline under `check_pipefail`. Import it qualified, since its names are the short ones a script reaches for.

```prism,no_run,mod=Shell
import Proc (..)
import Shell as Sh

fn main() : Unit ! {IO} =
  match run_proc(\() -> Sh.run_lines(command("git", ["status", "--short"]))) of
    Ok(changed) => println(Sh.unlines(Sh.grep(".pr", changed)))
    Err(e) => println(Sh.render(e))
```

The text helpers are pure: `lines`, `unlines`, `uniq`, `numbered`, and `grep` work on values a run already returned, so a script's filtering is ordinary code a test can call without spawning anything.

`unsafe_shell` is the one way to hand a string to the platform shell, and its name says so. No other function here parses, quotes, or expands a string.

## Types

### `ShellError`

```prism,def,h-8d09783bbfedea4788a7d8a5a0898d755800018e143ca48b9b935225a2cb4903
type ShellError = Failed(String, ExitStatus, Buf) | NotText(String)
```

A run that a script treats as failed: the program that failed, how, and its captured error stream; or a program whose output was not UTF-8 text.

### `unsafe_shell`

```prism,sig,h-3208f1f5a6556a432ae028ee1c2506229bf4b5f37fe10df6154331c0e6511eb5
unsafe_shell : (String) -> Proc.Command
```

A command that runs `script` through `platform_shell`, as `sh -c script`.

Use it only when a script needs what only a shell has: expansion, compound syntax, or a tool distributed as shell code. Three things follow from it, and none of them hold for `command`:

1. Text interpolated into `script` is shell syntax. A value that carries a quote, `;`, `$(...)`, or a newline runs as code, so a script built from input it does not control is a command injection. Nothing here quotes or sanitizes a string, because no quoting is right for every shell. 2. What `script` means is up to the platform shell: its quoting rules, builtins, and expansions differ between hosts and between shells. 3. It is not `command(program, arguments)`. The program the shell runs is found on the child's `PATH`, after the child's environment edits, and its arguments are words the shell split, not the list a caller wrote.

### `run`

```prism,sig,h-adce332993e37fe0b9f6aa5dd49a80144e6ea2c384489478dd79bc4dc2a82518
run : (Proc.Command) -> Result(Buf, Shell.ShellError) ! {Proc.Proc}
```


### `describe`


### `which`

```prism,sig,h-8447d5d6a8ddc2fd8b1fd6050e1ad8b6d1813bd060be72bbf2c495fa8fafe273
which : (String, List(Path.Path)) -> Option(Path.Path) ! {FileSystem}
```

The first directory in `dirs` holding a file called `name`, as that file's path. A `name` that is not a single path component is never searched for, and neither is a directory that is not absolute, as for `Proc`'s own search. The file is only known to exist: whether it may be executed is the host's answer when it is run.

### `search_path`

```prism,sig,h-8882d04c18ebdb49169be827e9dbdf9236344dbb6e9424b801a7ba926333e1c9
search_path : (String) -> List(Path.Path)
```

The absolute directories of a `PATH`-style value, in order. Empty and relative entries are dropped.

### `lines`

```prism,sig,h-ee13eb1f94ab312e45f501c23b83f1e687980fedfa4a0526372814a8166cae23
lines : (String) -> List(String)
```

The lines of `s`. A newline ends a line rather than separating two, so a final newline does not add an empty line and text without one still ends in a line. A carriage return is kept as part of its line.

```prism,mod=Shell
import Shell (lines)
lines("a\nb\n")
```

```output
[a, b]
```

### `unlines`

```prism,sig,h-44cd209831d6146a00c44d0583aae074f3421dde427d72eab2ed6f7a4bbddeac
unlines : (List(String)) -> String
```

`xs` as text, each line ended by a newline. `lines(unlines(xs))` is `xs` for lines without a newline of their own.

### `uniq`

```prism,sig,h-5d1323492afb695298325f1a29e8a834e9363850378598fb225379b173285193
uniq : (List(String)) -> List(String)
```

`xs` without adjacent repeats, as `uniq` prints them.

```prism,mod=Shell
import Shell (uniq)
uniq(["a", "a", "b", "a"])
```

```output
[a, b, a]
```
